instruction: Set the screen idle delay to 10 minutes (600 seconds) in the system settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);
import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.press('Escape'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('Escape'); time.sleep(0.2);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the idle-delay from 300 seconds (5 minutes) to 600 seconds (10 minutes). Verified that gsettings outputs format 'uint32 600\n' for this value.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts the GNOME idle-delay setting using 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay' - this is the correct command to read the system setting
Metric 'exact_match' correctly handles the type='rule' parameter: get_rule() returns config['rules'] directly, so metric receives {'expected': 'uint32 600\n'} and correctly accesses rules['expected']
Expected value 'uint32 600\n' is semantically correct and matches the exact output format of gsettings command for the value 600 seconds (metadata confirms this was verified)
Evaluator provides complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (set idle delay to 600 seconds) and evaluator checks exactly that
Data flow is correct: gsettings command reads persistent system setting → returns 'uint32 600\n' → exact_match compares strings → returns 1.0 if match, 0.0 otherwise

Practical feasibility: gsettings reads from GNOME's persistent settings database, not dependent on UI state. The postconfig closing Settings window does not affect verification as the setting is already persisted
Edge cases handled: if setting not changed (still 300), evaluator correctly fails; if command fails, get_vm_command_line returns None and exact_match returns 0.0
